name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B
purpose: General-purpose reasoning and chat model; the BF16 release is the starting point for customization (post-training, domain adaptation, quantization) and NVIDIA recommends the NVFP4 release for deployment.

license.name: OpenMDW-1.1
license.notes: LICENSE read ("Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES", OpenMDW-1.1 text, identical to the Poolside copy): permission "to deal in the Model Materials without restriction, including under all copyright, patent, database, and trade secret rights"; distribution requires keeping a copy of the agreement and the notices of origin; patent-suit termination clause; "no restrictions or obligations with respect to any use, modification, or sharing of any outputs". OpenMDW-1.1 text read in the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning repo LICENSE and on openmdw.ai: 'permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to deal in the Model Materials without restriction, including under all copyright, patent, database, and trade secret rights'; conditions are only to keep the agreement and notices when distributing, and termination if you sue over patent or copyright infringement by the materials; 'no restrictions or obligations with respect to ... outputs'.

architecture.drafter: MTP layers; DSpark and DFlash NVFP4 drafters
architecture.why_this_design: NVIDIA states: NVFP4 pre-training recipe on more than 20T tokens; MTP layers give richer training signals and, with asynchronous RL, speed rollouts; speculative decoding supported.

pc-16gb.variant: UD-Q4_K_M 25 GB, experts partly in RAM
pc-16gb.notes: 3 B active; Mamba keeps the KV small even at long context.

engine_support.notes: Same nemotron_h_moe family as Bolt (ArchId::NemotronHMoe is in Tona); Lightning not run by us. GGUF arch name assumed from that family, unverified.

benchmarks.name: AA Coding Index (aggregator mirror), NVFP4 listing
benchmarks.harness: aggregator mirror of the Artificial Analysis Coding Index, read 2026-11-19; no per-row dates; upstream AA pages not reachable

strengths: 1M context with a small Mamba KV; very fast per research/08
German, French, Spanish, Italian, Japanese named in the card
weaknesses: Behind Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on every row of NVIDIA's own table (MMLU-Pro 81.9 vs 85.6, BrowseComp 37.0 vs 48.7)
soft.behavior: Thinking toggled with enable_thinking (default on); T=1.0, top_p 0.95; no token-budget control described.
best_for: Very long inputs on small KV budgets
soft.maturity: NVIDIA: large vendor, quick cadence (Lightning, Bolt, Super VL within three months).

user_reports.summary: "Useless for coding": loses almost everywhere to Qwen, above all on SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench (matches NVIDIA's own table)

Independent port: 23 Mamba-2 layers, 23 MoE layers (128 experts, top 6, one shared expert) and six NoPE full-attention layers; 127 tok/s on one RTX 5090 with an 18 GB converted tree. The author warns that applying RoPE to the NoPE attention layers produces fluent garbage.
A user calls it useless for coding, losing to Qwen models by a large margin on SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench (strongly worded, no own measurements).

tona_fit.reason: OpenMDW-1.1 (text read) and a cheap long-context KV footprint (only six attention layers), but weaker than the Qwen 35B-A3B class on NVIDIA's own table and criticised for coding; no independent German score. Missing nemotron_h_moe support is only a blocker.
blockers: quality below Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on NVIDIA table

sources.note: aggregator mirror of the Artificial Analysis Coding Index, read 2026-11-19; no per-row dates; upstream AA pages not reachable
